name: justaluckydude
archetype: In-play sports taker reacting to game events
headline: Buys the side a scoring play (or another win-probability swing) just helped, within seconds, across college football, NFL, NBA, MLB and NHL. The reaction is real and identifiable, but every public-data version of it is not significantly profitable once a realistic information delay is applied, and the wallet's own profit is decaying.
mechanism: All sampled fills are taker fills. Within 10 s after a scoring play known 5 s after its ESPN wall clock, 95% of its buys favour the scoring side (other takers 60%). A reviewer rule reacting to any play that moves ESPN's win probability explains more: 36% of all its buys. Its profit is concentrated in college football and MLB; NBA, which dominated the held-out games, lost money. Half of the taker fees it pays come back as an Obsidian rebate.

roc.detail: 27%/month: 30-day PnL $138,804 on peak capital at risk $506,910; counting the on-chain collateral too ($532,394), at least 13%/month

onchain.detail: 200/200 sampled fills confirmed in Polygon OrderFilled events; 0% maker fills (95% CI 0%-2%), 0% of USDC

match.detail: direction after scoring plays 94.8% vs null 95th percentile 64% (perm p=0.005, 86 held-out games), but the wallet is not more reactive than other takers (11% vs 15% of fills in the window, p=0.73). Reviewer WP-REACT (any win-probability swing): AUC 0.648, p=0.005, 36% of buys - significant, but most decisions stay unexplained

backtest.detail: REACT(D=5 s, W=10 s) held out +1.1% (17,783 trades, p(profit)=0.40); zero-delay upper bound +4.4% (p=0.21); reviewer WP-REACT +3.2% (p=0.068); wallet's own fills on the same games +3.2% (p=0.25)

replicable.detail: the edge sits in the first seconds after a play; with a 5 s information delay the rule earns +1.1% (p=0.40) and reviewer WP-REACT goes to about zero at +5-10 s

persistence.detail: last 30 days not significant (p=0.15); significant negative trend (p=0.0077). [last 30 days p=0.15; decline vs earlier p=0.17; last 15 vs prior 15 p=0.29; trend p=0.0077]

reasons: The reaction signature is real but explains only part of its decisions; no rule meets the match bar.
No public-data version is significantly profitable on held-out games with a realistic information delay.
Its last 30 days are not significant and its daily PnL has a significant negative trend.
corrections: The earlier headline rule (D=0 s, W=20 s, +3.8%) assumed ESPN data arrives with no delay at all; refitted with a minimum 5 s delay it chooses D=5 s, W=10 s and earns +1.1% (p=0.40).
The earlier 'reactive share' p-value did not mean it reacts more than other takers; it does not (its distinguishing feature is direction).
30-day PnL includes a 50% taker-fee rebate; at the 0% tier it is $113,211 (still above $50k).
